summary:
Bounded first batch: a new in-tree driver directory linux/drivers/net/ethernet/lowrisc/ (Kconfig + Makefile + lowrisc_ethernet.c, upstream GPL/Xilinx/Microchip attribution kept in the file header), hooked into the parent Kconfig/Makefile, plus the three defconfig symbols and the two PLIC interrupt-cell fixes in configs/platform.dts. Nothing else is touched (no RTL, no other sources).

Driver scope actually implemented:
- probe: alloc_etherdev, timer_setup, devm_ioremap_resource of the 0x8000 window (size checked), platform_get_irq, MAC from DT via of_get_ethdev_address() (fallback: MACLO/MACHI read-back, else eth_hw_addr_random), programs MACLO/MACHI (network byte order) and RFCS=8 = lastbuf so the 8-slot ring is enabled; error paths unwind mdio -> napi -> free_netdev. remove(): unregister_netdev -> phy_disconnect + mdiobus_unregister/free -> netif_napi_del -> free_netdev.
- MDIO is a phylib bit-bang master (alloc_mdio_bitbang + mdiobb_ops) using readl/writel on 8-byte-aligned low halves of MDIOCTRL; MDIO_OE is handled as active-high drive (T = ~phy_mdio_oe), matching ariane_peripherals_xilinx.sv. phy_mask scans the strapped address only (default 1 = RTL8211E-VL, overridable by an optional DT 'phy-addr'); phy_connect() with PHY_INTERFACE_MODE_RGMII default (of_get_phy_mode() still wins), phy_set_max_speed(1000) + clear 1000baseT_Half so 10/100 links are never advertised or reported up. adjust_link() drives netif_carrier_on/off from real phydev->link/speed/duplex only - no faked carrier; an up-but-unsupported link keeps the carrier off.
- open/stop lifecycle: open = program MAC + flush stale RX ring (firstbuf := nextbuf) + request_irq + napi_enable + irq_enable + netif_start_queue + phy_start; stop = phy_stop + netif_stop_queue + napi_disable + irq_disable + free_irq + del_timer_sync + abort TX (TFCS write) + free pending skb. No mutex anywhere; only spin_lock_irqsave, so no sleeping in xmit/IRQ/NAPI/timer paths.
- ISR checks the real RX pending bit (RSR bit 12) and returns IRQ_NONE otherwise, masks the level-triggered source and schedules NAPI; the poll re-arms the source only after napi_complete_done().
- NAPI poll drains at most 'budget' slots, ring pointers are 4-bit with (buf & 7) slot indexing, RSR write of buf+1 acks a slot *after* the copy (so the MAC cannot overwrite the slot being read), lengths are validated (ETH_ZLEN..mtu+ETH_HLEN+ETH_FCS_LEN), and buffer transfers use readq()/writeq() with an exactly-len-byte memcpy on the CPU side, so no memcpy_toio byte writes and no overrun past len.
- TX: single buffer with a software busy guard (tx_skb) plus TPLR_BUSY polling; non-linear skbs are linearised (or dropped), the length is validated against both the MTU bound and TPLR bits 10:0, buffer writes are followed by wmb() before the length write that starts the frame, the queue is stopped while a frame is pending and woken by the timer (or by the inline poll), and ndo_tx_timeout(dev, unsigned txqueue) aborts via TFCS and frees the pending skb.

Known limitation explicitly documented in the driver header: this RTL exposes no per-frame RX error status (axis_gmii_rx's tuser/bad-FCS is not wired to the register file, there is no error counter register), so the driver deliberately does not report rx_crc_errors/rx_frame_errors and does not synthesise them.
assumptions: Patch paths are relative to the workspace root that contains 'iommu-platform/'; i.e. apply from there (git apply -p1 / patch -p1). If applied from inside iommu-platform/, strip the leading path component (use -p2 or sed the 'a/linux/...' prefixes).

KEY OPEN POINT / risk to verify against the RTL interface model: the RX length register RPLR is written by framing_top.sv as rx_length_axis[nextbuf] <= rx_addr_axis + 1, i.e. it counts every byte axis_gmii_rx pushes onto its AXIS output. Reading axis_gmii_rx.sv, that stream is payload + the 4 FCS bytes (STATE_PAYLOAD outputs gmii_rxd_d4 up to the cycle !gmii_rx_dv is seen, then STATE_CRC emits 4 more bytes with tvalid and asserts tlast on the last of them). Per the approved design boundary the driver therefore does NOT do 'len -= 4'; if the RTL model (or the actual eth_mac_1g_rgmii_fifo/rgmii_soc, whose source was not supplied) shows the FCS is still present in the stream, the single required change is: in lowrisc_poll(), use 'len -= ETH_FCS_LEN' (or accept only len >= ETH_ZLEN + ETH_FCS_LEN) right after reading LOWRISC_RPLR. If the FIFO does strip/drop bad frames (RX_FRAME_FIFO(1)) then no change is needed.

RX slot size / stride: slot index = buf & 7, slot byte offset = 0x4000 + (buf & 7) * 0x800, which is the addressing used with readq()/writeq() on the 64-bit port B of the RX RAM (addrb = core_lsu_addr[13:3]). This matches the original driver.
TX buffer is the 0x1000..0x1FFF window and holds at most one frame <= 1518 bytes plus zero padding to a 64-bit boundary; TPLR length field is 11 bits so the driver also rejects len > 2047.

TX has no completion interrupt. Completion = 'TPLR_BUSY seen set, then clear' (or 'clear after a full timer tick', because a <=1518 byte frame takes ~12 us). xmit additionally polls inline (up to 100 x udelay(1)) so the common case completes without a full timer tick; the timer (1 jiffy, re-armed while still busy) is the guaranteed queue-wake fallback and ndo_tx_timeout (2 s) is the watchdog. On a HZ=100 kernel the timer-only path would cap the rate at ~100 frames/s, which is why the bounded inline poll exists; Codex may drop the inline loop if a timer-only implementation is preferred.

PHY assumptions from the manual/straps: Realtek RTL8211E-VL at MDIO address 1, auto-negotiation, internal TX/RX RGMII delays off, MAC supplies the 90 degree TX clock, therefore phy-mode = rgmii. The driver defaults to PHY_INTERFACE_MODE_RGMII when the eth node has no phy-mode property; no phy-mode was added to platform.dts because the batch was limited to the interrupts=<2>/<3> fix. Only 1000BASE-T full duplex is advertised (fixed 125 MHz RGMII clock).

MAC address comes from the device tree (of_get_ethdev_address, i.e. the existing local-mac-address property); the boot-loader value in MACLO/MACHI and a random address are only used as fallbacks. The driver still writes the address into the hardware at probe and at open.
Optional DT property 'phy-addr' (u32) overrides the strapped PHY address; it is not present in platform.dts so the default 1 is used.

ethtool ndo_ioctl/phy_do_ioctl was deliberately not implemented (the old driver's MII ioctl used phy_read on an unlocked/possibly NULL PHY); phylib still provides SIOCGMIIPHY/REG through the PHY layer via ethtool get_link_ksettings and the PHY sysfs attributes.
configs/linux_defconfig additions: CONFIG_LOWRISC_ETH=y (selects PHYLIB and MDIO_BITBANG), CONFIG_REALTEK_PHY=y, CONFIG_SPI_XILINX=y; all pre-existing options are left untouched.

configs/platform.dts: only interrupts = < 2 2 > -> <2> in spi@20000000 (the SD/MMC-over-SPI node) and interrupts = <3 0> -> <3> in eth@30000000 are changed, so both match PLIC #interrupt-cells = <1> and irq_sources[1]/irq_sources[2]. The timer node is untouched.
Nothing was executed: no compile, no kernel build, no hardware test was run by this worker; the patch is a proposal for Codex to apply and verify.
checks: Apply: from the directory containing iommu-platform/, run 'git apply --check -p1 <patch>' (or 'patch -p1 --dry-run'), then apply and confirm only the 7 expected paths changed (3 new files under linux/drivers/net/ethernet/lowrisc/, ethernet/Kconfig, ethernet/Makefile, configs/linux_defconfig, configs/platform.dts).

Patch well-formedness: verify the new-file hunk headers (@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@ Kconfig, +1,6 @@ Makefile, +1,872 @@ lowrisc_ethernet.c) match the number of '+' lines; if git rejects a hunk count, recount rather than trusting this worker.

Config: regenerate with the target defconfig (make ARCH=riscv O=... linux_defconfig or the project's config target) and check CONFIG_LOWRISC_ETH=y, CONFIG_PHYLIB=y, CONFIG_MDIO_BITBANG=y, CONFIG_REALTEK_PHY=y, CONFIG_SPI_XILINX=y all resolve, and that Kconfig emits no 'select ... has unmet direct dependencies' warning.

Build: 'make ARCH=riscv CROSS_COMPILE=riscv64-linux-gnu- drivers/net/ethernet/lowrisc/' (and a full vmlinux build) against Linux 6.5-rc2; the API surface to watch is netif_napi_add(dev, napi, poll) (3-arg, v6.1+), ndo_tx_timeout(dev, unsigned int txqueue), of_get_ethdev_address(np, ndev) returning int, phy_ethtool_get/set_link_ksettings, phy_set_max_speed(), linkmode_clear_bit/linkmode_copy (pre-6.7 signatures), readq/writeq on void __iomem *.
Style: scripts/checkpatch.pl --strict on the new file and on the whole patch; expect no errors (warnings about the long copyright block should be the only possible noise).

Source review checklist (already believed satisfied, to be re-verified by Codex): no mutex anywhere; spin_lock_irqsave only; TPLR/RPLR/RSR/MACHI/RFCS access via 8-byte-aligned readl/writel; packet buffers only via readq/writeq with exactly-len memcpy; RSR ack (slot+1) happens after the copy; poll loop is strictly bounded by budget (drops and allocation failures also increment 'received', so the loop cannot spin forever under a RX flood); napi_disable() before irq disable/free_irq and del_timer_sync() before the TX state is cleared; ISR masks the source, poll re-arms it only after napi_complete_done().

RTL interface model checks (also usable as the 'necessary RTL interface model'): (1) a register write requires WSTRB[3:0] all set at an 8-byte-aligned low half; (2) writes to offset 0x830 load firstbuf, writes to 0x828 load lastbuf, writes to TPLR {tx_enable_dly<=10, tx_packet_length<=wdata} start a frame, writes to 0x818 clear it; (3) TPLR bit 31 = tx_busy mirrors 'tx_enable_dly != 0 || frame in flight'; (4) RPLR/RSR read back first/next/last/avail/irq as encoded in the driver's masks; (5) a 64-bit store to TXBUFF/RXBUFF updates both 32-bit halves (web = {|be[7:4], |be[3:0]}), proving a 32-bit or byte store is insufficient.

End-to-end on hardware/model once the driver builds: 'ip link set eth0 up' should show carrier off until the PHY reports 1000baseT full duplex; a ping of the board should show rx_packets/rx_bytes increasing with the expected frame lengths, and tx_packets increasing with the TX queue never permanently stopped (timer wake). Check /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/rx_errors stays 0 and that rx_fcs/rx_frame errors are never reported (the hardware cannot expose them).

Regression guard: verify the SD/MMC-over-SPI (interrupts=<2>) and eth (interrupts=<3>) nodes no longer produce a DTC/PLIC '#interrupt-cells' warning, and that the untouched timer node still boots with its 4-cell interrupts list exactly as before.
